chunks: a tall lad of swinging gait from Banū Thaqīf would be placed over you. He would eat away your vegetation and melt your fat.

key_terms.خَضِرَتَكُمْ: Your vegetation (metaphor for fresh wealth or vitality)
key_terms.شَحْمَتَكُمْ: Your fat (metaphor for accumulated wealth or richness)
key_terms.غُلاَمُ ثَقِيفَ: Lad of Thaqif (referring to a ruler from the Banu Thaqif tribe)

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'lad of Thaqif' mentioned in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Scholars traditionally identify this 'Ghulam Thaqif' as Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab, noting the specific descriptors 'thiqal' (heavy/stout) and 'mayyal' (inclined to ease/pleasure) as key indicators of his physical and administrative style. The phrase 'eating their greenery and melting their fat' metaphorically describes the extraction of wealth and vitality from the populace, a theme central to Shia critiques of early caliphal governance. This narration is frequently cited in eschatological discussions as a historical precedent for the transition from the Prophet's era to the subsequent political realities.

en.sayed-ali-raza: a tall lad of swinging gait from Banū Thaqīf would be placed over you. He would eat away your vegetation and melt your fat.
So, O Aba Wadhāḥah, is that all?
